equivalent: Equivalent by the arithmetic, not by what the suite happens to contain. The function returns None before this line for every even k and for k = 0, so k is ODD wherever `half` is computed. Write k = 2j + 1: then n = k - 1 = 2j, so n / 2 = j, while k / 2 = (2j + 1) / 2 = j in integer division. The two expressions are the same integer for every reachable input, including k = 1 (both 0) and k = usize::MAX (both (usize::MAX - 1) / 2, since usize::MAX is odd). `half` is used only as the bound of the loop that accumulates C(n, half) as a product of ratios, and nothing downstream reads it, so no operand, no operation and no order of operations changes. CHECKED, not asserted: the two forms were compiled side by side and compared with f64::to_bits on every k in 0..=200000 -- identical bit pattern at every one, None at every even k -- and (k - 1) / 2 == k / 2 was checked at 1, 3, (1 << 62) + 1, usize::MAX - 2 and usize::MAX. No test could tell: there is no input at which the mutated function returns a different value.
